title: Converge SDK error codes, exceptions, and actionable messages
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem
We currently have three SDK stacks (Python, TypeScript, Go) with divergent error shapes, inconsistent retry semantics, and varying developer ergonomics for streaming errors. This leads to confusion in integration code, duplicated retry logic in customers, and flaky behavior when the runtime surface returns intermediate or partial errors (streaming).

Goals
- Define a single error taxonomy and canonical payload shape emitted by the Redwood runtime and surface stable exception classes across SDKs.
- Provide clear, actionable messages and machine-friendly error codes so callers can: decide retry/no-retry, backoff windows, and remediation suggestions without parsing human text.
- Make streaming ergonomics first-class: allow consumers to distinguish recoverable stream updates vs terminal stream errors, and provide safe checkpointing hooks.

Out of scope
- Changing backend runtime error-generation semantics in this ticket (dependency ENG-8130 owns runtime-side code points). This work focuses on SDK surface and mapping.

Success criteria
1) A language-agnostic error spec merged in RFC form (Confluence) and agreed by SDK owners.
2) Prototype implementations for Python/TS/Go that: expose typed exceptions, include retry metadata, and support structured streaming error events.
3) Example app in examples/ that replaces ad-hoc retry code with the standardized helpers.

Design (high level)
Canonical error payload (JSON emitted by runtime, stable keys):
- code: stable string identifier (e.g. RI_RATE_LIMIT, RI_MODEL_CRASH, RI_BAD_REQUEST)
- numeric_code: integer (for compact telemetry and future mapping)
- message: short human-friendly summary
- detail: optional long-form diagnostic (stack snippets, model logs reference)
- suggestion: short actionable remediation (e.g., "reduce batch_size", "retry with exponential backoff", "contact support with ref")
- retryable: boolean flag as string in SDK metadata ("true"/"false")
- retry_after: seconds or RFC 1123 timestamp for when retry is allowed
- docs_url: link to internal docs / runbook
- incident_id: opaque UUID for correlation with infra logs

Principles and trade-offs
- Use explicit retryable flag rather than inferring from HTTP codes — avoids leaky mapping across transports.
- Keep message short at runtime; put large diagnostic payloads behind detail/docs_url to limit token cost in hosted responses.
- Provide both stable string codes (primary) and numeric codes for compact telemetry.
- Avoid throwing raw HTTP errors in higher-level SDK methods; always convert to typed SDK exceptions with the canonical fields.

SDK surface proposal (examples)
Python (catch and inspect):

try:
    resp = client.generate(prompt)
except RedwoodError as e:  # base class for all SDK errors
    if e.retryable == True:
        # helper will pick exponential backoff defaults from SDK config
        schedule_retry(e)
    elif e.code == "RI_RATE_LIMIT":
        wait_seconds = int(e.retry_after or 1)
        logger.info(f"Rate limit - retry after {wait_seconds}s")
    else:
        logger.error(f"Terminal error: {e.code} - {e.message}")

TypeScript (typed discriminated unions):

try {
  const out = await client.generate({ prompt })
} catch (err) {
  if (isRedwoodError(err)) {
    if (err.retryable) {
      retryWithBackoff(err)
    } else if (err.code === 'RI_MODEL_CRASH') {
      // escalate
    }
  }
}

Go (error wrappers):

resp, err := client.Generate(ctx, req)
if err != nil {
  if re, ok := RedwoodErrorFrom(err); ok {
    if re.Retryable {
      // use SDK backoff helper: sdk.RetryWithContext(ctx, func() ... )
    }
  }
}

Streaming ergonomics
- Streams will emit three event classes: data, progress, error_event. error_event is distinct from stream termination.
- Clients must be able to subscribe to on_error callbacks with full structured payload (same canonical fields).
- SDKs will provide a stream.Error type that contains whether the stream is resumable and a resume_token if available (for large response checkpointing).

Retries and idempotency
- SDK will provide a RetryPolicy object that understands error.retryable and error.code. Policy includes max_attempts, base_backoff, max_backoff, and jitter.
- For non-idempotent operations (e.g., log-probability consuming endpoints) SDK will refuse automatic retries unless caller supplies idempotency_key.

Telemetry and observability
- SDK should emit telemetry with numeric_code and incident_id.
- SDK will surface counters for retry attempts per error.code to console/metrics adapter.

Implementation plan (tasks)
1) Draft RFC and share with SDK owners and runtime (owner: Aisha) — DONE 2025-02-14 (link: https://confluence.redwood/rfcs/sdk-error-taxonomy)
2) Python prototype: convert HTTPError -> RedwoodError, add RetryPolicy helpers, unit tests (owner: Luca) — WIP, PR at https://github.com/redwoodinc/sdk-python/pull/276
3) TypeScript prototype: add discriminated error union, helper isRedwoodError, retry helpers (owner: Mei Chen) — In Review, PR #122
4) Go prototype: error wrapping utilities and RetryPolicy, streaming resume token support (owner: Sanjay Patel) — Blocked by ENG-8130 for runtime numeric codes mapping
5) Examples + docs: examples/error-handling/* and SDK docs page — pending

Progress updates
- 2025-02-18: Design review feedback: prefer string stable codes over free-form names (accepted). Add docs_url field to each error for runbook links (accepted).
- 2025-02-22: Python prototype implements RedwoodError base + subclass RateLimitError; includes retry_after mapping and helper retry_with_policy. Unit tests added.
- 2025-02-25: TS owner requested: make code and numeric_code both required to simplify telemetry ingestion. Added to spec.
- 2025-02-28: Cross-team sync: runtime team agreed to publish numeric mapping in ENG-8130 by 2025-03-07. This dependency is blocking Go streaming resume-token work.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Do we expose detail in error objects by default or behind a `verbose_errors` SDK flag? (Performance/token cost trade-off).
  - Proposal: default to minimal message + docs_url; `verbose_errors=true` opt-in for dev mode.
- Naming: prefer prefix RI_ for codes (Redwood Inference). Confirmed in design review.
- Retry semantics for streaming partial errors: should SDK automatically try to resume?
  - Proposal: SDK exposes resume_token but leaves automatic resume to higher-level helper to avoid hidden side effects.

Risks
- If runtime numeric mapping slips, SDK telemetry will be inconsistent. (Dependency ENG-8130).
- Customers relying on textual messages could break if we remove important context; must provide clear migration docs.

Next steps (short term)
- Ship Python and TS prototypes to beta customers; collect feedback (owner: Luca / Mei) by 2025-03-12.
- Finalize Go mapping once ENG-8130 lands (owner: Sanjay).
- Draft migration guide and example patterns for streaming error handling.
